summary.headline: Northern Arc posted record Q4FY26 PAT of INR133 crore (up 251% YoY) and FY26 PAT of INR406 crore, with AUM at INR16,594 crore (up 22% YoY).
summary.overview: Northern Arc reported its highest-ever quarterly profit of INR133 crore in Q4FY26, taking FY26 PAT to INR406 crore (up 33% YoY). AUM grew 22% YoY and 10% QoQ to INR16,594 crore, with direct-to-customer (D2C) at 59% of AUM. Credit cost fell to 2.2% in Q4 (from 3.5% in Q3) and 2.8% for FY26, helped by the RBI's FLDG-related ECL clarification, which management said contributed a one-off benefit. Management guided FY27 AUM growth of 22-25% and ROA above 3%, with ROE in the mid-to-late teens over 8-10 quarters.

financial_highlights.change: FY26 +34 bps YoY; Q4 +66 bps QoQ
FY26 -48 bps YoY; incremental vs 9.3% a year ago

financial_highlights.value: INR12,258 crore (Mar 2026); ~INR12,900 crore cited later in call

segments.name: Direct-to-customer (D2C)
segments.commentary: D2C AUM about INR9,800 crore (+39% YoY), 59% of total AUM, targeted to reach 65%. Management expects the mix shift to support NIM expansion.

segments.name: Consumer finance
segments.commentary: AUM above INR5,000 crore, growing about 50% in the year per analyst; 70% repeat customers; risk-adjusted yield targeted at 15-16%; ROA stated as upward of about 4%. Short-tenure book reduced to near zero, and an APR cap introduced.

segments.name: MSME (incl. LAP)
segments.commentary: Portfolio INR3,691 crore, up about 43% YoY, with 17 new branches in FY26. X-bucket collection efficiency 99.4% in March 2026; average ticket INR11-15 lakh; yield 17-18%.

segments.name: Rural finance (MFI)
segments.commentary: AUM INR1,009 crore (+8% QoQ); record quarterly disbursement about INR305 crore (+17% QoQ); 64 branches added, network about 342; X-bucket collection efficiency 99.6%. MFI is 6% of AUM; 84% of MFI book covered under CGFMU.

segments.name: Credit solutions / fee business
segments.commentary: FY26 placement volume INR11,834 crore with placement fee income up 22% YoY to INR31 crore; credit fund AUM INR3,092 crore earning about INR38 crore fee in FY26. Securitisation placed about INR10,000 crore last year.

guidance_outlook: FY27 AUM growth of about 22-25% (about 3x GDP), described as a commitment to the Street barring a major shock.
Target ROA of 3%+ and ROE of mid-to-late teens within 8-10 quarters (analyst recap of 15-17% in about two to two and a half years was accepted by management as 15-17%).
FY27 credit cost guided at 2.7-2.8%, after adjusting for FLDG benefit and INR66 crore management overlay.
Cost of funds expected to hold at about 8.5-8.6%; no further reduction expected, with D2C mix expansion expected to improve yields.
Consumer finance risk-adjusted yield to hover at 15-16%; MSME growth to be more cautious given competition and stress risk.
capex_capacity: Added 66 branches and merged two during Q4FY26; 17 MSME branches added in FY26.
Rural network about 342 branches after adding 64 in the quarter.

Management plans to keep investing in distribution, talent, infrastructure and technology; rural exposure was cut from about INR1,500 crore to about INR900 crore in late FY25 and is now being rebuilt.
Affordable housing product board-approved; launch deferred until LAP business reaches scale.
Capital adequacy 22.6% gives headroom to grow the balance sheet over the next two to three years.
demand_pricing: Consumer finance: about 25,000-26,000 loans disbursed per day, tied to consumption demand.
MSME: management said the segment has a credit gap of nearly 24% (about INR30 lakh crore) but flagged rising competition and recalibrated merchant lending.
MFI market described as stabilising; management expects this to aid placement and fee lines.
Exposure to MSME sectors exposed to the West Asia conflict (gas, petrol, chemicals, pesticides) is under 2% of book, per management.
Partner base of 368 originating partners; 90% rated BBB or above.

qa_highlights.question: What FY27 loan growth and ROA guidance is being given, given the evolving macro?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided 22-25% AUM growth (about 3x GDP) and a 3%+ ROA target, with mid-to-late teens ROE in 8-10 quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there risk building in MSME merchant lending and consumer finance, which grew about 50%?
qa_highlights.answer: Consumer finance is underwritten via scorecards with a 15% risk-adjusted return; MSME average ticket is INR11-15 lakh, yield 17-18%, all with 100% registered mortgage. Management acknowledged the small base inflates growth rates.

qa_highlights.question: Why has ECL coverage fallen, particularly Stage 2 and Stage 3?
qa_highlights.answer: The RBI FLDG clarification (Feb 2026) let the company count FLDG cover in ECL; over 50% of Stage 2 is FLDG-covered. Stage 3 is now mainly secured MSME, given 100% write-off of unsecured loans at 90 DPD.

qa_highlights.question: Is the FLDG reversal one-off, and what is the underlying Q4 credit cost?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the Q4 FLDG benefit was INR29 crore and the INR66 crore overlay is prudence. Adjusting for prior-year provision, the underlying Q4 credit cost would have been about INR120 crore (about 2.9-3%), with 2.7-2.8% as steady state.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for cost of funds and NIM given rate movements?
qa_highlights.answer: Fixed-rate share rose from about 30% to 40%; incremental CoF 8.7% vs 9.3%; management expects to hold 8.5-8.6% and NIM to expand as D2C mix rises to 65%. Management expects RBI rate increases in the next couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Is there concentration among consumer finance partners, and what is the asset quality and yield?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said yield is 15-16% risk-adjusted; short-tenure book cut to near zero; APR cap introduced; no partner concentration figure given in the call.

qa_highlights.question: Why has bank borrowing share fallen while bank lending to NBFCs has risen?
qa_highlights.answer: Bank borrowings fell from about 65% of total in March 2025 to about 52% in March 2026, with more offshore, capital market and securitisation (PTC) funding.

risks_watch: Credit cost sustainability: FY27 guidance of 2.7-2.8% depends on FLDG-adjusted provisioning and the INR66 crore overlay; Q4 benefit included a one-time component.
West Asia conflict, monsoon and macro stress flagged by management; MSME competition and merchant lending risk.
Rising hedge costs and G-Sec yields (about +50 bps) and possible RBI rate hikes could pressure cost of funds beyond the 8.5-8.6% guide.
Borrowing figures differ in the call (INR12,258 crore vs about INR12,900 crore); verify in the filings.
Management did not give quarterly credit cost by segment in the presentation; analyst requested it.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on profitability, asset quality and FY27 growth, with repeated caveats on West Asia tensions, monsoon and macro risk. Management was more evasive on the one-time nature of the FLDG benefit and on the mechanics of credit cost, requiring follow-up clarification from the Group Risk Officer.
key_quotes: Our sense is we should be able to grow business at about three times of GDP, so look at anywhere between 22% to 25%, and that's our commitment to the Street on a forward -looking basis unless we see something massive.
It's pure organic, except for the DLG that we spoke about, but ap art from that there is no one-off.

Adjusted for all this, the actual the credit cost without the overlay and adjusted for all this would have been closer to around 120 crores, which would have been much closer to the 2.9% to 3%, the which we would have otherwise got.
I think we will definitely not see a reduction in the cost of fund, but we will be able to hold on to the numbers that we have demonstrated this year.
The bank borrowings used to be close to about65% of my total borrowing in March 25, this has consciously come down to around 52% as we speak in March 26.
